contract.purpose: Assign group/spot and optionally rename a container and its direct children.
inputs_defaults: renameContainer bit, assignSpot bit, groupNum nvarchar(50), contId nvarchar(25), internalContNum numeric(9), spotNumber numeric(9), required. No defaults.
null_and_invalid_input_behavior: NULL flags do not take equality-to-one branches. NULL spot becomes zero. NULL target ID updates nothing but still returns a spot. No group, ID uniqueness or warehouse validation is present.
output_shape: One scalar result set containing the final spot number.

ordered_branches.explanation: If assignSpot=1 and spotNumber=0, compute MAX related group position plus one through work transport-container IDs. Convert NULL spot to zero.
Update selected container and direct children: always set GROUP_NUM, set GROUP_POSITION only when assignment requested and spot positive.
When renaming, replace CONTAINER_ID only for parentless rows and PARENT_CONTAINER_ID only for positive shipment-line rows; return computed/provided spot.

contract.status_and_quantity_effects: Only the explicitly described persistent writes occur in this body.
configuration_scope_and_precedence: The supplied selectors govern this body. No separate effective setting or cross-layer precedence is established; configuration values were not queried.
error_and_return_handling: No custom TRY/CATCH, THROW or failure return is implemented. SQL conversion, constraint and dependency failures propagate to the caller.
contract.transaction_ownership: No explicit BEGIN/COMMIT/ROLLBACK transaction, savepoint, TRY/CATCH or XACT_ABORT is introduced. Caller/session transaction semantics govern effects.
concurrency: MAX+1 is not protected by serializable locking; concurrent callers can derive the same position. Related work lookup does not include a warehouse predicate.
contract.trigger_behavior: Persistent DML may activate configured table triggers; transitive trigger/caller behavior is separate from the direct body.
external_handoffs_and_gaps: Application call binding, permissions, active deployment, complete process duration and downstream behavior are not established by this static contract.

NO_CAPTURED_REFERENCE means none of the credited channels in this exact retained corpus identified the table. It does not establish that the table is unused, obsolete, a backup, safe to delete, or absent from external application SQL.
Dynamic SQL, runtime-selected identifiers, external callers, client-generated SQL, uncaptured jobs and historical/other database code can use tables without a resolvable reference here.

The bounded lexer recognizes named SQL relation/DML positions and local aliases/CTEs; it is not the SQL Server binder. Unqualified names assume a unique captured name, not verified caller/default-schema resolution. Unsupported or ambiguous syntax remains explicit.
